drivingQuestion: In what circumstances did they suckle from a kosher animal on a Festival?
outcomeNote: The practice concerns suffering without danger; the reason Festival differs is given in the next unit.

segments.he: אַבָּא שָׁאוּל אוֹמֵר: נוֹהֲגִין הָיִינוּ שֶׁיּוֹנְקִים מִבְּהֵמָה טְהוֹרָה בְּיוֹם טוֹב. הֵיכִי דָּמֵי? אִי דְּאִיכָּא סַכָּנָה — אֲפִילּוּ בְּשַׁבָּת נָמֵי, וְאִי דְּלֵיכָּא סַכָּנָה — אֲפִילּוּ בְּיוֹם טוֹב אָסוּר! לָא צְרִיכָא דְּאִיכָּא צַעֲרָא.
segments.en: The Gemara analyzes the last opinion in the above baraita. «Abba Shaul says: We were accustomed to suckle from a kosher animal on a Festival.» The Gemara inquires: «What are the circumstances? If there is» imminent «danger» to a person, «even on Shabbat» it should «also» be permitted. «And if there is no danger, even on a Festival» it should be «prohibited.» The Gemara answers: «No,» it is «necessary» in a case «where there is suffering,» i.e., they suffer from thirst but no danger is involved.
